facts.claim: Language identifiers/display names should live in a single parser-free registry module, derive the TypeScript union type from it, and be re-exported for all consumers (storybook, pickers, downstream features) instead of maintaining parallel hardcoded lists that must be kept in sync by hand.
facts.evidence: `CodeMirrorEditorLanguage = keyof typeof CODE_MIRROR_LANGUAGES` in types.ts, with languages.ts comment: 'Keep the registry free of parser imports so consumers can read language metadata without loading language code.' This replaced duplicated arrays in CodeEditor.story.tsx, languageLoader.test.ts, and codeLanguages.ts.

facts.claim: Deriving downstream lists from the shared registry removes a previous compile-time exhaustiveness guard (a Record keyed by the union type) that forced a compile error when a new language was added without a label, trading that safety net for less duplication.
facts.evidence: Removed comment: 'A Record rather than an array so adding a ninth language to CodeMirrorEditorLanguage fails to compile here until it is given a label, instead of silently missing from the picker.' replaced by `const HIGHLIGHTED = Object.keys(CODE_MIRROR_LANGUAGES);`

facts.claim: Legacy/StreamLanguage-based CodeMirror language support (e.g. INI via @codemirror/legacy-modes) can be added as a lazy-loaded extension by combining StreamLanguage.define with a legacy mode import, following the same webpackChunkName lazy-import pattern as native @codemirror/lang-* packages, without requiring changes to the loader test's language-agnostic structure.
facts.evidence: `loadIni` imports `{ LanguageSupport, StreamLanguage }` from `@codemirror/language` and `{ properties }` from `@codemirror/legacy-modes/mode/properties`, returning `new LanguageSupport(StreamLanguage.define(properties))`, registered via the same `resolveLoad` switch/cacheKey pattern as other languages.

json.reason: The PR demonstrates a concrete refactor pattern (single source-of-truth registry replacing duplicated hardcoded arrays/Records across multiple files), an explicit tradeoff noted in removed comments (losing a compile-time exhaustiveness check), and a reusable mechanism for adding StreamLanguage-based (legacy-mode) language support lazily alongside native CodeMirror language packages. These are durable, mechanism-level lessons about this codebase's CodeMirror language extensibility architecture, not generic styling or narration.
